edges.effect_quant: Prospective cohort data suggest a clinically meaningful but not extreme effect, especially in higher-risk or more exposed groups.
edges.mechanism: Exogenous estrogen, and especially estrogen-progestin combinations, can stimulate proliferation in hormone-responsive tissues while also changing clotting, lipids, and systemic inflammation. That makes the balance of benefit and harm for Endometrial cancer highly dependent on tissue type, duration, and timing relative to menopause.
edges.summary: Prospective cohort data link estrogen-only menopausal hormone therapy to higher risk of endometrial cancer in postmenopausal women with uterus. The average effect is usually moderate rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
